= Real-estate MLS search: metasearch, `libresearch.space`, and authorized RESO access =

**Reviewed:** 2026-11-04
**Interpretation:** “MLS” means a real-estate Multiple Listing Service.
**User decision (2026-11-04):** public-web discovery only; do not build an MLS/RESO integration.
**Method:** GitHub repository metadata, READMEs, source files, the project-maintained SearXNG instance registry, and GitHub-hosted uptime snapshots. No live search query was run against `libresearch.space` or another public instance because direct access to non-GitHub hosts is unavailable in this workspace.

== Bottom line ==

- `libresearch.space` is a **public SearXNG instance** listed by the SearXNG project. Its root was reported up with HTTP 200 in the instance-monitoring repository’s latest per-instance record. The same repository showed **100% uptime over its last 30 days and a 202 ms 30-day response-time summary** at the snapshot reviewed.
- A public GitHub mirror of the operator’s NixOS configuration has a bot-protection rule that **challenges `/search` requests** (while allowing the SearXNG instance checker by address). This is not a live test and may have changed, but it means the good root-page uptime does not establish that automated search/API requests will work without a challenge.
- Among alternative public instances sampled from the same monitor, none was both faster and more available over the last 30 days. `baresearch.org` had slightly higher monitor-reported uptime over its full observation window, but was slower; those full-window values are not directly comparable because monitoring start dates differ.
- None of this establishes search-result quality, available search engines, privacy practices, or ability to return current MLS inventory. `libresearch.space` can help with **public-web discovery**, not replace licensed MLS data.
- For current, queryable listing inventory, the stronger route is the relevant MLS/provider’s authorized **RESO Web API / IDX feed**, with permission and compliance with that feed’s license and display rules. An open-source client or sync tool does not itself grant MLS data access.

== What `searx.space` and `libresearch.space` are ==

`searx.space` is the SearXNG project’s statistics/directory for public instances, not itself an MLS search service ([project repository snapshot](https://github.com/searxng/searx-space/tree/94dfa9c0e29694268b4a64ac68e052750f1ec035)). The project’s [public-instance registry file](https://github.com/searxng/searx-instances/blob/05924e97a4629fe5c4cd345977060e25ed75ac9b/searxinstances/instances.yml) contains `https://libresearch.space` as a listed instance. The registry entry has no special MLS/data-feed capability indicated.

The [SearXNG instance uptime repository](https://github.com/searxng/searx-instances-uptime/tree/e3c269585608076983da69e8c6517499cb2e4777) records this for `libresearch.space`:

- Last per-instance record reviewed: `2026-11-04T02:51:56Z`
- Probe result: HTTP `200`, `97 ms`
- Monitor start time: `2026-08-15T12:53:13Z`
- Monitor-reported uptime: `99.61%` since monitoring started; `100%` for the last 30 days
- Monitor-reported 30-day response-time summary: `202 ms`

The “1y” badge generated by the monitor should **not** be read as a full year of observation: the per-instance history says monitoring started on 2026-08-15. The monitor URL is the site root, so this status probe is an availability check, not a search-quality or `/search` endpoint test.

=== Search-path bot challenge in a public configuration mirror ===

A public GitHub mirror of an operator NixOS repository contains configuration for `libresearch.space` ([reviewed snapshot](https://github.com/nuclear-gumbo/nixos/tree/ebc3fdab55a24aa30342b5fe7dee97f41a05e291); see `machines/server/srv-n2/containers/anubis.nix` and `searxng.nix`). The Anubis policy in that snapshot allows the SearXNG instance checker by address, allows non-search paths, and sets `/search` requests to **CHALLENGE**; the SearXNG configuration also enables its limiter. This is a source-configuration finding, not proof that the live deployment still behaves exactly this way. It does, however, warn against treating the root uptime check as proof that automated JSON/API searches will succeed. Do not attempt to bypass the challenge; use a self-hosted instance or a provider-supported API for programmatic work.

=== Public-instance comparison ===

A small comparison using metrics published in the same SearXNG uptime repository:

| Instance | Monitor-reported last-30-day uptime | Last-30-day response-time summary | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `libresearch.space` | 100% | 202 ms | Fastest response-time summary in this sample. |
| `baresearch.org` | 100% | 308 ms | Higher observed all-window uptime (99.91%), but a different monitoring window and slower 30-day response. |
| `etsi.me` | 100% | 323 ms | No measured advantage in this sample. |
| `search.rhscz.eu` | 100% | 622 ms | No measured advantage in this sample. |
| `paulgo.io` | 99.55% | 705 ms | Lower recent availability and slower response in this sample. |

These are snapshots of third-party monitoring, not independent tests. They do not establish that one instance returns better results, offers the same engines, is suitable for sensitive queries, or is permitted for automated/high-volume use. **There is no evidence here that switching from `libresearch.space` to one of these public instances would improve MLS search.**

== How a general metasearch engine can help—and where it stops ==

SearXNG combines results from upstream web-search providers. This can help find public brokerage pages, IDX pages, county records, market reports, or documentation. It does **not** crawl and maintain a complete independent MLS inventory, and it does not confer a right to access, retain, index, or republish MLS data. Listings may be missing, stale, de-indexed, or subject to a site’s access and display terms.

For sensitive searches or repeatable research, self-hosting SearXNG gives more control over the metasearch service, but not over the upstream engines it queries: search terms are still sent to those providers. The SearXNG project is AGPL-3.0 and was actively updated at the reviewed snapshot ([source commit](https://github.com/searxng/searxng/tree/cccbc9e158b0ac3bb2158e9841a647a5bec57b57)). Self-hosting is a privacy/control option, not an MLS data-access workaround.

=== Alternatives reviewed ===

- **Whoogle:** Its own README says that upstream blocking stopped results and active development ended on 2026-07-24. Although the repository is MIT-licensed, it is not a good current working alternative ([reviewed repository snapshot](https://github.com/benbusby/whoogle-search/tree/0543f86528678ab60a20b3049483975add6b6e40)).
- **RustXNG:** A self-hosted Rust implementation based on SearXNG. Its README explicitly says it does not maintain an independent index, sends queries to selected upstream providers, and that provider terms/permissions must be checked; some adapters are disabled pending permission review. It is not proven to return better MLS results ([reviewed snapshot](https://github.com/sahenjp/RustXNG/tree/9e77a1377a2443f859d75d27f11742028a66f1cf)).
- **Vane** and **Morphic:** AI-answer/search applications that can use SearXNG and/or other providers. They may help synthesize public-web research, but they add an LLM/API layer and do not supply licensed MLS records or canonical inventory. They are not replacements for RESO access.

== MLS/RESO access is a separate authorization problem ==

The relevant repositories illustrate the distinction:

| Project | Purpose and constraints | Appropriate role |
|---|---|---|
| [MLS Grid Sync](https://github.com/piotrsenkow/mlsgrid-sync/tree/73ddbc2eeae220e8d8a782ab5435b6581c669105) — Apache-2.0, v0.1 | Replicates MLS Grid / RESO Web API feeds into PostgreSQL. Its project documentation says a data-license agreement and approval for each MLS feed are required; the software includes neither MLS data nor credentials. | A possible authorized-feed ingestion component after the provider grants access; not a way to obtain access. |
| [openresync](https://github.com/tylercollier/openresync/tree/7fedd4e06558198645ec0659296edf301aafc432) — MIT, alpha | Syncs RESO Web API data to MySQL or Solr. The author reports production use with feeds, but the project is still explicitly alpha and each data source is separately authorized. | A technical reference or candidate connector after feed access is approved. |
| [WFRMLS client](https://github.com/theperrygroup/wfrmls/tree/1b3b51102083ac01544948b8f9c4f67df6a64ac8) — MIT | Provider-specific UtahRealEstate.com/WFRMLS client requiring a provider-issued token and permission. | A provider-specific example, not a nationwide MLS client. |
| [RESO Web API reference server](https://github.com/RESOStandards/reso-web-api-reference-server/tree/cd9b5663c99407c90aac552ebbcecc0b124017bf) | Standards/reference implementation for development and testing; not a production MLS feed or source of listings. No SPDX license was returned in the reviewed repository metadata. | Protocol/testing reference only. |

The sync-tool documentation is not a substitute for the controlling data license or local MLS rules. Before implementation, verify allowed fields, attribution, display, refresh, caching/retention, derivative use, deletion on revocation, and downstream redistribution with the specific MLS/data provider.

== Recommendation ==

1. **For interactive public-web discovery:** `libresearch.space` is worth trying for non-sensitive searches, but expect that `/search` may present an anti-bot challenge; this is inferred from a public configuration mirror, not live-tested. The monitor data gives no reason to switch to the sampled public alternatives on latency/availability alone. For programmatic searches or privacy/control, self-host SearXNG or use a provider-supported API and review the enabled upstream engines and their terms.
2. **For actual MLS inventory search (outside this request):** the technical route would be the target MLS/provider’s authorized RESO Web API/IDX access and an approved client/adapter, with provider rules followed. The user selected public discovery only, so no MLS/RESO integration is being designed or built here.
3. **Do not scrape or use metasearch as a workaround** for missing MLS authorization. Public search results are not a comprehensive or authoritative feed.
4. **Do not assume Directory Desk should sync remotely.** Its existing local/offline constraint remains in force; this research does not authorize sending contact, badge, or MLS data to an external service.

== Limits of this review ==

- The live `searx.space` and `libresearch.space` sites were not directly accessed from this workspace. The instance identity and uptime figures above come from GitHub-hosted project registries/monitor files, not a live interactive search test.
- No query was run to measure result relevance, enabled engines, MLS-domain coverage, logging, or rate limits.
- No MLS geography/provider or feed agreement was supplied; because the user chose public discovery only, no MLS integration was attempted and credentials are neither needed nor requested.
- Uptime and response-time checks measure availability/latency only. They are not evidence that a public instance is safe for confidential searches or that its upstream sources permit a particular automated use.
